title: Privacy, security and AI assurance
text: **Collect data for a defined purpose**

pages.title: Data minimization and purpose
text: **Collect data for a defined purpose**

Data minimization begins by identifying what each product function needs. A service engineer may require a calibration trend and hardware version without needing patient identifiers. A measurement algorithm may require a plate image whose label region contains information irrelevant to analysis. The design should reduce unnecessary exposure at the point of collection and use.
## Proposed purpose map

Each data class should have a documented purpose, authorized roles, retention basis and permitted onward use. Clinical operation, service diagnostics, product improvement and research are distinct purposes that may require different permissions and agreements.
## Preserve useful lineage without excessive disclosure

Pseudonymous identifiers can support linkage within an authorized workflow while limiting routine access to direct identifiers. The reidentification mapping should have its own access controls. Pseudonymization is not the same as anonymization, because the relationship may still be recoverable.

The proposed platform should make purpose restrictions enforceable through permissions and data flows. A broad statement that all available repositories will train an AI would be inconsistent with this approach. Curated, licensed and purpose-specific access can support useful research while preserving the rights and responsibilities attached to each source.

pages.title: Consent and lawful data use
text: **Lawful use must be assessed for the actual data flow**

The legal and ethical basis for collecting, storing and reusing data depends on jurisdiction, institutional roles, purpose and the nature of the information. A laboratory's permission to process a specimen does not automatically authorize every form of commercial model training or onward sharing. The proposed programme should document these distinctions before data collection.
## Current Indian planning context

India's final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 provide phased commencement. The Gazette distinguishes provisions commencing at publication, after one year and after eighteen months. Applicable obligations, corrections and other relevant law must therefore be checked for the deployment date and processing arrangement. This compendium describes design intentions, not a legal compliance determination. [R54]
## Build controls that support the decision

The system should retain evidence of the applicable permission or agreement without exposing unnecessary personal information. Research datasets need approval and access records appropriate to the study. A change in purpose should trigger reassessment rather than being treated as covered by a historical generic permission.

The deployment team should obtain qualified legal and institutional review for the specific arrangement. Technical safeguards support lawful processing, but encryption or pseudonymization alone does not establish that a proposed use is authorized.
tables: Separate clinical, service, research and model-development purposes.

pages.title: Identity access and authorization
text: **Authorization should be enforced where the data are accessed**

Authentication establishes an identity; authorization determines what that identity may do. The proposed platform should enforce permissions on the server or equivalent trusted boundary, including direct requests for records, images, exports and administrative actions. Hiding a button in the interface is not an access control.
## Proposed role separation

Laboratory reviewers, operators, service staff, researchers and administrators may need different privileges. Access should follow the minimum scope required for the task and be reviewed when responsibilities change. Shared accounts weaken accountability and should not be the default for consequential actions.
## Test the denied paths

Verification should attempt access through direct object identifiers, stale links, alternate routes and lower-privilege sessions. A successful authorized request does not demonstrate that unauthorized requests are rejected. Signed links and cached files need expiry and scope consistent with the intended access policy.

Session revocation, account recovery and emergency access should have defined behavior. The system should preserve essential audit evidence while avoiding disclosure of credentials or secrets in logs. Controlled external review of a product document or research dataset should use an explicit audience and should not accidentally expose the same material through a public route or search index.
tables: Restricted technical data and time-bounded support access.

pages.title: Encryption and key management
text: **Encryption depends on key management and endpoint controls**

The proposed system should protect sensitive data in transit and at rest using established, appropriately configured cryptographic mechanisms. Encryption is one layer of protection. An authorized application with excessive access, a compromised endpoint or an exposed key can still disclose encrypted information after decryption.
## Proposed key lifecycle

Keys and credentials should be provisioned through controlled mechanisms, stored outside source code and ordinary logs, rotated where appropriate and revoked when no longer authorized. Recovery arrangements must avoid making a single lost key the cause of permanent loss of required records.
## Include devices and removable media

An instrument may retain images or queued records during offline operation. Its local storage and service access need protection appropriate to the data. Exported files can also leave the application's controls, so the export workflow should identify the recipient, purpose and permitted handling.

The engineering specification should use current supported security mechanisms and independent review rather than inventing a custom encryption scheme. Verification should include configuration and operational procedures, not only the presence of an encryption library. The product claim should describe the implemented protection accurately without suggesting that encryption makes the system immune to compromise.

pages.title: Secure software development
text: **Security engineering should be part of ordinary development**

The proposed software lifecycle should include threat modelling, secure design, dependency management, code review, verification and vulnerability response. Security requirements should follow the product's assets and trust boundaries. Medical-device cybersecurity guidance and health-software security standards provide relevant planning references, with applicability assessed for the intended product. [R49] [R53]
## Track the software supply chain

A software bill of materials identifies relevant components and versions. It supports vulnerability assessment and change management but does not itself prove security. The team should determine whether a reported vulnerability is reachable in the product and what mitigation or update is needed.
## Test the AI-specific boundaries

Retrieved documents and user-supplied text should not gain authority to change permissions or execute actions. A language assistant needs constrained tools, source-aware responses and explicit authorization for consequential operations. Training and evaluation should include misleading instructions embedded in otherwise relevant material.

Security findings should enter the same controlled change process as other product defects, with priority based on impact and exposure. The proposed programme should retain unresolved risks and support periods transparently. A clean automated scan is useful evidence for the checks performed, not a guarantee that no exploitable weakness exists.

pages.title: Instrument and network security
text: **Instrument security includes physical and network boundaries**

An instrument connects software to a physical laboratory workflow. Security assessment should consider local storage, service ports, removable media, update mechanisms and network access. A protected cloud service does not compensate for an instrument that exposes records or accepts unauthorized control locally.
## Proposed deployment boundary

The device should expose only the services needed for its qualified functions. Network segmentation, authenticated communication and controlled administration can limit unnecessary reachability. Remote support should be explicitly authorized, scoped and auditable, with a defined end to the session.
## Safe operation during isolation

If a security incident requires network isolation, the instrument should enter a defined operating mode. It may retain eligible local capture and review or suspend functions that depend on trusted external services. The choice must follow the qualified workflow and risk assessment, not an improvised response during an incident.

Verification should include unauthorized control attempts, invalid updates and loss of network trust. The product should preserve record integrity and avoid unsafe physical actions when communication fails. Security and biological reliability interact: an incident that changes timing, calibration or environmental control may require assessment of affected laboratory records as well as restoration of the software.

pages.title: Incident response and recovery
text: **Incident response should restore trustworthy service**

The proposed incident process should identify, contain, investigate and recover from events affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability. Recovery is complete only when the system and relevant records are trustworthy for their intended use. Restarting a service without assessing altered data or configuration can leave the underlying problem unresolved.
## Proposed response record

The team should preserve the incident timeline, affected systems, observed indicators and actions taken. Access to evidence should be controlled, and sensitive information should not be copied into broad support channels. Notification obligations depend on the applicable law, agreement and incident context.
## Test restoration before it is needed

Backups should be tested for completeness, integrity and usability, including required keys and configuration. Recovery objectives should reflect the laboratory workflow and retention requirements. A backup that exists but cannot be restored within the needed context is not an effective continuity measure.

Exercises should include corrupted records, lost credentials, unavailable cloud services and instrument replacement. After restoration, the system should reconcile queued events and identify uncertain intervals. Affected approvals or interpretations may require review if their inputs or integrity cannot be established. Incident closure should retain the evidence and residual limitations rather than merely marking the service online.

pages.title: Privacy in shared research datasets
text: **Research sharing should preserve utility while limiting disclosure**

A research dataset may contain direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, labels embedded in images and sensitive institutional information. Removing a name field is not sufficient to establish anonymity. The proposed sharing process should assess what can be inferred from the combination of fields and the recipient's access to other information.
## Proposed dataset release process

The release should have a defined purpose, authorized recipients, permitted analyses and retention conditions. Data minimization should be applied to images, metadata and free text. The team should verify that transformation has preserved the scientific variables required for the study.
## Treat transformed data as a new release

The dataset should retain a version, transformation description and relationship to the authorized source. Researchers need to know whether values were removed, generalized, imputed or simulated. Privacy transformations can affect analytical validity and should be considered in interpretation.

The proposed programme should use institutional and legal review appropriate to the data and jurisdiction. A public repository's availability does not automatically authorize every reuse or combination. Shared research should return useful scientific value while respecting the original permissions and avoiding claims that a technical de-identification step guarantees zero reidentification risk.

pages.title: AI assurance and change management
text: **AI assurance continues after the first evaluation**

An AI capability needs a defined intended use, data lineage, performance assessment and change process. Assurance also includes behavior under uncertainty, shift and misuse. General AI risk-management and good machine-learning-practice resources provide useful principles, but they do not certify a particular model or replace product-specific evidence. [R21] [R23]
## Proposed model release record

The record should identify the model, training data release, preprocessing, decision thresholds and evaluated domain. It should retain conventional baselines and known limitations. The interface and downstream rules that use the model are part of the evaluated system configuration.
## Monitor without uncontrolled learning

Field monitoring can identify drift, unexpected failures and review patterns. It should not automatically convert every user correction into a training label or update the deployed model continuously. Candidate changes need curation, evaluation and controlled release.

The proposed system should support rollback to a qualified version while preserving which version produced each historical output. Monitoring should include accepted-case errors, abstention, data quality and important subgroups. A stable average score can conceal changing case mix or a local failure. Assurance therefore requires interpretable evidence and accountable decisions throughout the model's service life.
